I'll start by reading the docs and inspecting the code.

Output was truncated; I'll read the middle of the spec and the rest of the docs.

My last call was cut off before it ran. I'll make the edits one at a time instead.

Next, `text.py`: grouping by `group_sizes` and `min_grouping`, and the date patterns.

That call was cut off too. I'll write `text.py` with `write_file` instead.

`strftime("%Y")` doesn't zero-pad years below 1000 on Linux, so I'll format the canonical datetime text explicitly.

That edit came out convoluted, so I'll replace it with something plain.

Now I'll run the unit tests and some spot checks.

The output looks right: en-IN grouping gives `5,00,291`, and the split file names follow the spec. I'll clean up and write the status file.

The `export` command is finished and follows `docs/export.md`. One existing test still fails because it contradicts the spec.

`python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` runs 28 tests, and 27 pass. The failing one is `test_split_into_files` in `tests/test_export.py`. It expects `people-001.csv`, but spec section 10.3 requires `people.slice-001.csv`. I followed the spec, as I'm not allowed to change the tests.

I also ran `export` by hand on the real store with several options. Locale grouping, null placement and split file names looked right. I did not run a full check of every option combination against the spec.

What I fixed or wrote:
- **Filtering:** `--where` is now evaluated. It was a stub that raised `NotImplementedError`. Nulls make comparisons false, and `not` flips true and false.
- **Locale text:** date and datetime patterns now work, using the longest-token rule and the 12-hour clock. Digit grouping now follows the locale's `group_sizes` and `min_grouping`. It was hard-coded to groups of three, which gives the wrong result for `en-IN`. Years are zero-padded.
- **CSV output:** the quoting rules are now my own code instead of Python's `csv` module, which didn't match the spec. Records end in CR LF, the null token is never quoted, and a value equal to the null token is quoted.
- **Sorting:** `:nulls-first` and `:nulls-last` were being reversed by `:desc`. They now stay fixed whatever the direction.
- **Splitting:** split files are named `name.slice-NNN.ext`. The suffix starts at the last `.` unless it is the first character, and numbers are three digits or wider.
- **Store reader:** in `tally/store/store.py`, `Collection._lines` used `str.splitlines()`. That could cut a record in two on characters like U+2028 inside a JSON string. It now splits on `\n` only, which also affects the other commands.

`/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success` and a summary that mentions the conflicting test.

command_result.command: cd /app && cat docs/overview.md docs/conventions.md docs/export.md && find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | grep -v __pycache__ | head -100

cd /app && for f in tally/export/*.py tally/commands/export.py tally/commands/__init__.py tally/commands/query.py tally/cli.py tally/textio.py tally/errors.py tally/where.py tally/sorting.py tally/store/*.py tally/fmt/locales.py tally/fmt/numbers.py tally/fmt/dates.py; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done; git status 2>&1 | head

cd /app && for f in tally/export/expr.py; do sed -n 150,400p $f; done; for f in tally/export/text.py tally/export/order.py tally/commands/export.py tally/commands/__init__.py tally/commands/query.py tally/cli.py tally/textio.py tally/errors.py tally/store/schema.py; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done

cd /app && cat tally/commands/export.py tally/commands/__init__.py; sed -n 1,60p tally/store/store.py; cat tests/test_export.py | head -80; cat tests/support.py; cat locales/de-CH.json locales/en-IN.json locales/ja-JP.json

cd /app && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -20; python -m tally export orders --locale en-IN --columns id,total,placed --sort total:desc:nulls-first --max-rows 1000 2>&1 | head -5; python -m tally export orders --locale en-IN --columns id,total,placed,paid --sort paid:desc:nulls-first --null NA | head; cat store/orders/schema.json | head -30

cd /app && python -m tally export orders --locale en-IN --columns id,total,placed,discount_rate --sort discount_rate:desc:nulls-last,id --null NA --where "status is not null and not total < 100000" | head -8 | cat -A | head -8; python -m tally export orders --locale de-CH --columns id,total --where "total > 1000000" --no-header | head -3; python -m tally export customers --out /tmp/x/a.b.csv --max-rows 7 --columns id; ls /tmp/x

rm -rf /tmp/x; cd /app && cat > STATUS.json <<'EOF'
{"status": "success", "summary": "Finished the export command: implemented --where evaluation, locale date/datetime patterns and group_sizes/min_grouping grouping, spec-exact CSV quoting with CRLF, null placement independent of direction, .slice-NNN file naming, and made the store reader split lines on newline only. One existing test (tests/test_export.py test_split_into_files) still expects the old people-001.csv naming, which contradicts spec section 10.3; I followed the spec and did not touch the tests."}
